overview: A good spread of marks with no evidence of time pressure; several questions tested practical skills from the AS course.
Marks were lost through imprecise definitions, incomplete working and not answering the question set.
Stronger candidates gave detailed reasoning, logical working, correct technical terms and handled graphs and uncertainties confidently.
Weaker candidates omitted calculation steps, missed or misused units and conversions, and were unsure interpreting graphs and uncertainties.
In 'show' questions make the method explicit with the unknown as the subject; working back from the given value earns no credit.
assessment_for_learning: For gradients: mark coordinates that lie on the line (not table points), use a triangle at least half the line length, read axis units and powers of ten, and show (y2-y1)/(x2-x1).
Gradient of a velocity-time graph is acceleration; area under it is displacement.
Velocity is a vector - include direction (sign) when sketching or calculating.
For repeated readings, absolute uncertainty is half the range.
Practise estimating everyday physical quantities (e.g. mass of an adult).
When reading from a graph, check the scale and units on each axis.
Use the OCR Practical Skills Handbook for planning-question guidance.
